Here’s an overview of the Prisma AIRS Terminal codebase, based on verified facts about its structure and functionality:

## High-Level Description

- **Prisma AIRS Terminal** is a Rust-based local terminal application that acts as a coding assistant.
- It interfaces with a remote AI gateway for language inference, but runs its shell agent, TUI (terminal user interface), and workflow management locally.
- The repository URL is [https://github.com/cdot65/prisma-airs-terminal](https://github.com/cdot65/prisma-airs-terminal).

## Main Directory Structure

The repository is organized as a Rust workspace with these primary directories:

- **cli/**: The actual terminal entrypoint. This package contains code to launch the CLI application, parse arguments, and initialize the local environment.
- **tui/**: Implements the interactive terminal UI. This is where text-based user interfaces, live interaction flows, and command feedback are handled.
- **core/**: Contains the agent runtime, which manages task execution, prompt routing, tool invocation, context caching, subprocess handling, and workflow logic.
- **mcp-scanner/**: (Separate from the above) Implements an optional remote scanner backend, likely for integration with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) resource/tool system.

## Key Capabilities

- Can execute shell commands and manage subprocesses within a controlled sandbox on your local machine.
- Integrates with the “Model Context Protocol” (MCP) for resource and tool access across AI-enabled workflows.
- Supports skills—structured local instruction sets (via SKILL.md) for workspace- or agent-level actions, document generation, plugin scaffolding, and more.
- Honors strict sandboxing and escalation policies for filesystem and command execution permissions.
- Can connect to remote backends (AI gateways) for LLM inference, with selectable providers/models if configured.

## What It Doesn’t Do (by Default)

- It does **not** run the large language model locally—the AI reasoning is always routed through the configured remote gateway.
- It doesn’t provide deep learning or direct model manipulation capabilities on the local machine.
- It operates independently from the package hosted in your current workspace; the source checkout and any running deployment are not linked unless you explicitly connect them.
